method: Fresh read-only primary-source inspection and bounded equivalent-statement searches; no priority guarantee.

sources.title: Private Algorithms Can Always Be Extended
sources.comparison: General factor-two extension is prior theory. It does not state the optimized reservoir peak or the exact cost of coordinate endpoint-range restrictions.

sources.title: Gaussian Differential Privacy
sources.passages: Theorem 2.10, Theorem 2.14, Proposition 2.15 and the latter proof
sources.comparison: Blackwell comparison and the continuous-group Laplace limit are credited background. None of the three accepted proofs needs a new unrestricted-reachability claim.

sources.title: Unique geodesics for Thompson's metric
sources.comparison: Cone Thompson uniqueness and section Hilbert uniqueness have different hypotheses and metrics. The candidate's fixed-time uniqueness follows directly from saturation of both changing binary coordinates, not from an ambient-space uniqueness inference.
sources.access: Primary PDF text accessible. Screenshot requests returned cache misses; no visual review of this source is claimed.

sources.title: Interpolation-Based Optimization for Enforcing lp-Norm Metric Differential Privacy in Continuous and Fine-Grained Domains
sources.comparison: Normalization is explicit and Proposition 3 accounts for its factor-two cost. This does not assert that normalized coordinates remain between their endpoint probabilities. The frozen theorem makes no contrary attribution.

sources.title: A Graph-Based Framework for Extending Metric Differential Privacy Mechanisms
sources.passages: Section 5.2 calibrated pre-normalization budget; Appendix E endpoint envelopes and normalized log-convex construction
sources.comparison: Endpoint envelopes and budget calibration are prior ingredients. The candidate's additional optimization is a cap on an individual normalized output throughout an entire path. No new general envelope principle is accepted.

sources.title: Software for the Thompson and Funk Polygonal Geometry
sources.comparison: Maximum forward/reverse Funk distance and ball intersections are prior constructions. They do not supply the path-constrained frontier. Endpoint distance and the length metric of its infinitesimal symmetrization must remain distinguished.

sources.title: Shape And Structure Preserving Differential Privacy
sources.comparison: These passages concern private estimation on Riemannian manifolds and preservation of geometric data shape, rather than coordinate endpoint ranges along probability paths. No full-paper exclusion is claimed.

sources.title: Reachable sets under Kolmogorov dynamics in the probability simplex
sources.comparison: A fresh additional comparison: its diagonal-infinity control gives the one-sided instantaneous cost max over negative velocities of |v_i|/p_i. The candidate uses the maximum of that cost in both velocity directions before taking path length. Symmetrizing the optimized endpoint quasi-distance does not perform this operation. No all-budget peak or sharp endpoint-range penalty is stated in these passages.

search_families: Thompson metric probability simplex intrinsic length and geodesics
coordinate-monotone and range-preserving differential privacy interpolation
mandatory probability excursions and interpolation overshoot
limits: No equivalent frontier or exact shape-penalty statement was located in these inspected primary passages and search results. Older constrained-control and function-algebra literature were not exhaustively screened. Failed access is not evidence of nonexistence.
